title: CaMDN: Enhancing Cache Efficiency for Multi-tenant DNNs on Integrated NPUs
problem: Multi-tenant DNN execution on shared SoC NPUs suffers from cache contention that degrades performance; shared cache impact on multi-tenant scenarios not well studied.
motivation: Multi-tenant DNN deployment on mobile/edge SoCs is becoming prevalent; uncontrolled cache interference between models creates unpredictable performance and prevents efficient resource sharing.
method: Multiple AI models running at the same time on a chip's shared cache compete for space, degrading performance. This approach uses three techniques: hardware support for dedicating cache regions to each model (controlled by the NPU, the processor managing the models), mapping that adapts based on available capacity, and dynamic reallocation that adjusts which model gets which region in real time as their demands change.
key_novelty: The core idea is a joint hardware-and-software design using NPU-controlled exclusive cache regions with dynamic allocation to prevent multiple AI models from competing for shared cache.
contributions: Lightweight hardware architecture supporting model-exclusive cache regions
Cache-aware mapping method adaptable to varying available capacity
Dynamic runtime allocation algorithm for multi-tenant cache sharing
33.4% average memory access reduction; up to 2.56x model speedup (1.88x average)
limitations: Specific DNN models, cache sizes, and tenant count configurations not detailed; scalability to extreme multi-tenancy (>8 models) not discussed.
primary_theme: Multi-tenant DNN cache efficiency via hardware-software co-design
